experiments.title: Research intake and read-only scene baseline
experiments.question: Can an agent distinguish source claims, installed capabilities and observed asset state without mutating the scene?
experiments.hypothesis: Hashed base-geometry/rig/material/action observations will expose silent changes that count-only checks miss.
inputs: Two completed research exports kept private
prerequisites: Existing LAS Python; no Torch import
Pinned installed Blender; never infer alpha API from release label
Native load-memory admission before the first process

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Import reports and verify archive integrity
Pin source, executable and probe bytes with plan-probe
Admit one read-only job through the native owner, with 120-second timeout and retained logs
Repeat on the same copy, then the existing compatibility anchor where that file format is supported
Compare semantic observations; do not open alpha-saved authoring sources in an older runtime
success: Exact intake round-trip
Repeated identical recorded semantic content
Seeded same-count connectivity change detected
No source hash change
experiments.stop: Stop on budget/API failure or source mismatch; never replace a missing observation with zero counts.
experiments.next_decision: Qualify the probe on a simple owned prop first; only then admit a private character copy.

experiments.title: Controlled source/candidate/export view evidence
experiments.question: Can silent export losses be localized without trusting one attractive render?
experiments.hypothesis: Identical camera/light/render contracts plus source and reimport images catch deliberately omitted geometry, texture loss and material drift.
inputs: Six canonical cameras plus two hold-outs
prerequisites: Scene probe qualified on selected runtime
Existing articulated/native-export owner
New evidence renderer and target-specific object mapping; not implemented by offline comparator

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Freeze rig, resolution, lighting, frame and color management
Render source and unchanged rerun to measure noise
Export with existing settings; reimport into a fresh process
Restore the external validation rig and render the same views
Seed omitted part, missing texture and shader-color changes in disposable copies
Compare and attribute differences, retaining intentional exclusions explicitly
artifacts: Per-view PNGs, scene observations, SHA-256 manifest
Raw comparison JSON and human review
success: All three seeded defects detected
Unchanged rerun lies within preregistered tolerance
Hold-outs present; unknown differences remain visible
experiments.stop: Stop if matching requires resizing, changing cameras or widening thresholds after seeing a failure.
experiments.next_decision: Promote technical gates only after repeatability; keep aesthetic acceptance independent.

experiments.title: Fine-grained 2D edit and editable-source roundtrip
experiments.question: Can agents change an intended region while preserving everything else and all editable layers?
experiments.hypothesis: Exact protected-region comparison plus native layer reopening is more dependable than whole-image similarity scores.
inputs: Small fixed set of repaint proposals
prerequisites: Existing Krita/native-copy workflow
Existing ComfyUI environment only if generation is separately admitted
Mask-aware comparison adapter; scalar full-frame comparator alone is insufficient

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Hash original layered source and record layer/mask/offset inventory
Apply one explicit masked edit or imported proposal in a copy
Reopen in Krita and export at the same native resolution
Require exact protected pixels and unchanged protected-layer inventories
Review the edited region at full size and intended presentation size
success: Zero changes outside the authorized mask
Editable layers survive reopen
Human approves the changed region
experiments.stop: Stop on layer flattening, hidden protected-pixel changes or a missing source mask.
experiments.next_decision: Expose a narrow mask-scoped edit command, never a general overwrite action.

experiments.title: Projection-to-UV portability closure
experiments.question: Can a selected projected paint layer survive the actual runtime export?
experiments.hypothesis: A bounded UV bake with coverage/seam evidence can separate unobserved surfaces from shader translation loss.
prerequisites: Selected Blender already installed
Portable target shader profile chosen
View parity capture implemented

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Inventory projection dependencies without modifying source
Bake one channel at 1024 square initially
Retain visibility/coverage and seam masks
Use image-based material on experiment copy only
Export/reimport and compare canonical plus hold-out views
success: All intended visible regions covered or explicitly classified as unseen
No unexplained export dropout
No new seams accepted by a global average metric
experiments.stop: Stop if a view-dependent effect cannot be baked faithfully; split authoring and runtime effects instead.
experiments.next_decision: Accept a portable material derivative or document a deliberate engine-specific implementation.

experiments.title: Pinned AMD workload benchmark
experiments.question: Which existing runtime/backend improves a real workload without a quality or memory regression?
experiments.hypothesis: Warm/cold-separated timing and memory receipts are sufficient to choose lanes without globally upgrading software.
inputs: Existing ComfyUI graph and fixed model pins
prerequisites: Exact existing Blender and Python environments
Existing resource admission/probe/receipts
A working telemetry source or explicit unavailable markers

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Choose at most four cases; keep GPU inference and Blender mutually scheduled through existing admission
Measure cold startup separately
For each case run three warm-ups and five measured repeats with identical seeds/settings
Capture wall time, peak observed memory, warnings and output evidence
Report median, spread and p95 only where sample count justifies interpretation
success: Repeatable workload-specific signal above run-to-run noise
No visual/functional regression
Memory measurements available or explicitly unknown
experiments.stop: Stop on out-of-memory, driver instability or conflicting live GPU work; never call a tiny probe a benchmark.
experiments.next_decision: Change only a workload profile with demonstrated benefit; do not upgrade drivers/ROCm by default.

experiments.title: Persistent worker necessity and recovery test
experiments.question: Is process startup a material bottleneck after useful asset work is included?
experiments.hypothesis: A persistent typed worker is worthwhile only when reduced overhead outweighs state and recovery complexity.
prerequisites: Existing headless owner as baseline
No new MCP server
Persistent process remains an isolated prototype

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Time fresh-process inspect calls and a proposed minimal persistent transport
Alternate assets A/B/A; verify semantic snapshots
Inject process crash, stale request and timeout
Measure useful work, startup overhead and recovery separately
success: At least 30 percent end-to-end improvement on the selected iteration workload
No A/B state leakage
Deterministic fallback to a fresh process
experiments.stop: Stop if only empty ping improves, source state leaks or recovery loses job identity.
experiments.next_decision: Build typed worker only after evidence; adapt the existing MCP surface rather than adding a second server.

experiments.title: Procedural prop and defect benchmark factory
experiments.question: Can editable procedural assets provide both useful outputs and a ground-truth agent test corpus?
experiments.hypothesis: Parameter-constrained generation with seeded topology/UV/material defects yields more useful automation evidence than text-to-3D demos.
prerequisites: Existing authored-prop adapter
Scene observation and controlled-view path
No external models or asset services

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Generate a small parameter sweep with source provenance
Seed one defect per copy including same-count connectivity changes
Measure detection and repair by category
Produce one LOD derivative with silhouette checks
Import one accepted technical candidate into an explicit target profile
success: Known defects detected without pristine fixtures falsely failing
Source remains editable
Measured intervention lower than manual repetitive delivery
experiments.stop: Stop if benchmark shortcuts expose labels to the agent or procedural variety lacks downstream usefulness.
experiments.next_decision: Expand a useful asset class; do not generalize to autonomous hero-character modelling.

experiments.title: Local visual critic calibration and counterfactuals
experiments.question: Can an available local model identify technical defects without overriding artistic decisions?
experiments.hypothesis: Narrow region-specific questions, human labels and hidden hold-outs outperform a single global quality score.
prerequisites: Separately pinned existing multimodal runtime/model or explicitly approved provider
No subscription/API availability assumption
GPU admission shared with rendering

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Record category, region, confidence and evidence for every prediction
Split tuning/hold-out assets, not merely adjacent frames
Test monotonic response to texture loss, occlusion and topology defects
Compare category precision/recall and calibration against human labels
success: Useful held-out technical defect precision/recall
No promotion from aesthetic score
Counterfactual failures remain visible
experiments.stop: Stop using any category with poor calibration or identity drift; do not increase authority to compensate.
experiments.next_decision: Admit only validated advisory categories; human acceptance remains external.

experiments.title: Synthetic constrained corrective-shape study
experiments.question: Can a small permitted deformation basis improve held-out stress poses?
experiments.hypothesis: A 10-parameter, topology-preserving solver on an owned synthetic rig can test whether inverse fitting is useful without unconstrained sculpting.
inputs: Owned synthetic rig, not a private character lead
Six training and four held-out poses
prerequisites: Topology/UV identity checks
Explicit geometry loss and displacement bound
Separate project authorization; do not run in a workspace that prohibits score-led sculpting

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Define constraints and displacement caps before optimization
Use bounded derivative-free search before CUDA-dependent tooling
Evaluate contact/silhouette/volume on training and held-out poses
Retain every candidate and failure
Convert only an accepted result into an ordinary authored corrective
success: Held-out geometric improvement without identity/topology drift
Manual artist finds the corrective useful
No runtime solver dependency required to use output
experiments.stop: Stop on training-view-only improvement, implausible compensation, licensing ambiguity or project-policy conflict.
experiments.next_decision: Continue as a synthetic research track or discard; private artistic workflows require a new explicit decision.

experiments.title: Hybrid mesh/neural reference stage
experiments.question: Does a reconstructed representation improve a concrete authoring task over ordinary image references?
experiments.hypothesis: A small rights-clean splat or reconstructed object can help camera alignment and proxy geometry even when the deliverable remains an editable mesh.
inputs: Self-owned or permissively licensed small capture
prerequisites: Exact installed feature probe for import/render support
External reconstruction is separately scoped; no CUDA-on-AMD assumption
No new paid/cloud route by default

budget.enforcement: Planning caps only; existing LAS admission and execution owners must enforce actual runs.

steps: Record representation provenance and exact importer capability
Align proxy geometry using image references as control
Repeat with the neural representation
Compare alignment effort, occlusion errors, memory and editability
Keep Blender authoring, importing and rendering roles distinct
success: At least one useful task beats image-plane baseline
Occlusion and performance limitations characterized
Editable mesh deliverable survives the workflow
experiments.stop: Stop when unstable import or CUDA-only reconstruction dominates the benefit; never silently rent a GPU.
experiments.next_decision: Retain as a specialized reference worker or reject without migrating the main authoring runtime.
